1.why: Verification compares the submitted code/token only to the reset secrets stored on that session, which is bound to the accountId/identifier set at recovery-request.

2.why: Reset codes live on one session only; another user/session has different manualCode/resetToken values, so the same code does not authenticate them.

3.why: password-change updates the account hash and current session stage but never deletes or invalidates other entries in the sessions Map.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HTTP is rejected via x-forwarded-proto, though a minimum TLS version is not explicitly pinned in code.

5.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but resetToken, manualCode, mfaCode, and identifiers are kept as plaintext fields in in-memory Session objects.

6.why: There is no real email channel; recovery codes and verification URLs are returned in the API JSON and mirrored into browser logs unmasked.

7.why: Inputs are allowlist-validated (validId/validCode/validPass) and the client assigns all dynamic strings with textContent only, never innerHTML.

8.why: verificationPath/URL are built as same-origin /verify?token=... on localhost; no user-controlled external redirect target is accepted.

9.why: No email HTML templates exist; mock delivery uses textContent log lines without interpolating user input as HTML or scripts.

10.why: manualRecoveryCode, verificationUrl, and testMfaCode are intentionally shown in the Logs panel and console, so tokens appear in logs.

11.why: Account passwords use bcrypt, but MFA_CODE is the plaintext constant "246810" embedded in source and INITIAL_PASSWORD_HASH is also hardcoded.

12.why: A pre-seeded helena@example.com account with a fixed demo bcrypt hash and hardcoded MFA code act as default/demo credentials.

13.why: allowed/fail implement progressive per-action, per-identifier, per-IP lockout delays (up to 5 minutes) on recovery, verify, mfa, password, and login.

14.why: Unknown identifiers are assigned sinkId and still get a generic recovery response; login failures always return the same non-enumerating message.

15.why: manualCode and resetToken are produced with crypto.getRandomValues (base64url) per recovery request and stored only on that user/session.
